mcqs.question: Consider two vectors A and B. Vector A has magnitude 10 units and makes an angle of 30° with the positive x‑axis. Vector B has components (8 i, 6 j). Which statement is true?

options.A: The x‑component of A is greater than the x‑component of B.
options.B: The magnitude of B is greater than the magnitude of A.
options.C: The y‑component of A is greater than the y‑component of B.
options.D: The direction of B makes a smaller angle with the x‑axis than vector A.

mcqs.answer: The x‑component of A is greater than the x‑component of B.
mcqs.explanation: For vector A, the x‑component is 10 cos30° = 8.66 units, which is larger than B's x‑component of 8 units. The other statements are false: both vectors have the same magnitude (10 units), A's y‑component (5 units) is smaller than B's (6 units), and B's direction (≈36.9°) is larger than A's 30°.

mcqs.question: A force of magnitude 25 N acts at an angle of 53° above the positive x‑axis. What are its rectangular components (Fx, Fy)?
mcqs.explanation: Fx = 25 cos53° = 25 × 0.6 = 15 N; Fy = 25 sin53° = 25 × 0.8 = 20 N. Hence the components are (15 N, 20 N). The other options correspond to incorrect trigonometric values.

mcqs.question: If a vector has components Fx = 6 N (along +x) and Fy = 8 N (along +y), which gives the magnitude and direction (θ measured from +x) of the original vector?
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude = √(6²+8²) = 10 N. Direction θ = tan⁻¹(Fy/Fx) = tan⁻¹(8/6) ≈ 53.1°. Options B, C, and D use incorrect magnitudes or angles.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: Which situation is best solved by resolving a vector into its perpendicular components?

options.A: Determining the net work done by a constant force when the displacement is at an angle to the force.
options.B: Calculating the speed of a car moving in a straight line.
options.C: Finding the mass of an object using a balance scale.
options.D: Measuring the temperature change of a gas during an isochoric process.

mcqs.answer: Determining the net work done by a constant force when the displacement is at an angle to the force.
mcqs.explanation: Work = F·d = Fx dx + Fy dy, which requires the force (or displacement) to be broken into perpendicular components. Options B, C, and D do not involve vector resolution.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes “resolution of a vector into components” from “projection of a vector on an axis”?

options.A: Resolution gives two perpendicular components that together reproduce the original vector, whereas projection gives only the component along a specified axis.
options.B: Resolution and projection are identical processes; both give the same numerical values.
options.C: Projection yields components that are always larger than those obtained by resolution.
options.D: Resolution can be performed only for vectors in the plane, while projection works in three dimensions.

mcqs.answer: Resolution gives two perpendicular components that together reproduce the original vector, whereas projection gives only the component along a specified axis.
mcqs.explanation: Resolving a vector produces both x‑ and y‑components that vectorially add to the original. Projection extracts only the component along a chosen direction. The other statements are false.

mcqs.question: A displacement vector of magnitude 13 m makes an angle of 37° with the positive x‑axis. What are its rectangular components (Δx, Δy)?
mcqs.explanation: Δx = 13 cos37° ≈ 13 × 0.8 = 10.4 ≈ 10 m; Δy = 13 sin37° ≈ 13 × 0.6 = 7.8 ≈ 8 m. Option A matches the rounded components. Other options correspond to swapped or incorrect values.

mcqs.question: A vector has components (−3 i, 4 j). Which statement is true?

options.A: Its magnitude is 5 units and it points 126.9° measured counter‑clockwise from the +x‑axis.
options.B: Its magnitude is 7 units and it points 53.1° measured clockwise from the +x‑axis.
options.C: Its magnitude is 5 units and it points 53.1° measured counter‑clockwise from the +x‑axis.
options.D: Its magnitude is 7 units and it points 126.9° measured clockwise from the +x‑axis.

mcqs.answer: Its magnitude is 5 units and it points 126.9° measured counter‑clockwise from the +x‑axis.
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude = √((-3)²+4²) = 5. The vector lies in the second quadrant (negative x, positive y). Angle from +x = 180° − tan⁻¹(4/3) ≈ 126.9°. Options B and D use an incorrect magnitude, and C gives the wrong quadrant angle.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: A projectile is launched with an initial speed of 20 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal. Which pair correctly gives the horizontal and vertical components of the initial velocity?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component = 20 cos30° = 20 × 0.866 ≈ 17.3 m s⁻¹; vertical component = 20 sin30° = 20 × 0.5 = 10.0 m s⁻¹. Option B swaps the components, C assumes 45°, and D ignores the angle.
